mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes a solenoid?

options.B: A coil of wire wound in a helix shape
options.C: A pair of permanent magnets placed side by side

mcqs.answer: A coil of wire wound in a helix shape
mcqs.explanation: A solenoid is a length of insulated wire wound tightly in a helical (coil) form. When current passes through it, the coil produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet. Option B matches this definition, while the other options describe different objects.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand magnetic field of a solenoid
mcqs.question: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is:

options.A: Uniform and parallel to its axis
options.B: Radial and outward from the centre
options.C: Non‑uniform and strongest at the ends
options.D: Zero because the wires cancel each other

mcqs.answer: Uniform and parallel to its axis
mcqs.explanation: For a long solenoid, the magnetic field lines inside are parallel to the axis and have nearly the same magnitude throughout, giving a uniform field. Outside the solenoid the field is very weak. Hence option A is correct; the other statements describe incorrect field patterns.

mcqs.question: An electromagnet differs from a permanent magnet because:

options.A: It does not produce any magnetic field
options.B: Its magnetic field can be switched on or off by controlling the current
options.C: It is made only of iron and cannot contain other metals
options.D: It is always stronger than any permanent magnet

mcqs.answer: Its magnetic field can be switched on or off by controlling the current
mcqs.explanation: An electromagnet consists of a coil of wire (often wound around an iron core). When electric current flows, a magnetic field is produced; removing the current makes the field disappear. This on‑off capability distinguishes it from a permanent magnet, whose field is always present. Options A, C and D are false statements.

mcqs.question: Which combination will produce the strongest electromagnet?

options.A: Few turns of thick wire with low current
options.B: Many turns of thin wire with high current
options.C: A single turn of thick wire with high current
options.D: Many turns of thick wire with low current

mcqs.answer: Many turns of thin wire with high current
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field of an electromagnet is proportional to the product of the number of turns (N) and the current (I). More turns and higher current give a stronger field. While wire thickness affects resistance, the key factors are N and I, making option B the best choice. The other options either have fewer turns or lower current.

mcqs.question: Which of the following devices uses an electromagnet to operate?
mcqs.explanation: An electric bell contains a coil that becomes magnetised when current passes, attracting a metal arm to produce the ringing sound. This is a classic application of an electromagnet. The other items listed contain no electromagnet components.

mcqs.question: A student wraps a long insulated copper wire tightly around a nail, connects the ends to a battery, and the nail becomes magnetic. Which part of this arrangement is the solenoid?

options.C: The coiled wire around the nail
options.D: The switch used to complete the circuit

mcqs.answer: The coiled wire around the nail
mcqs.explanation: The definition of a solenoid is a coil of wire. In the described experiment, the coiled wire is the solenoid; the nail acts as a ferromagnetic core, and the battery provides current. Therefore option C correctly identifies the solenoid.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand magnetic field of a solenoid
mcqs.question: A common misconception is that the magnetic field outside a long solenoid is as strong as the field inside. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The external field is equally strong as the internal field
options.B: The external field is negligible compared to the internal field
options.C: The external field is stronger than the internal field
options.D: There is no magnetic field outside the solenoid at all

mcqs.answer: The external field is negligible compared to the internal field
mcqs.explanation: For a long solenoid, the magnetic field lines are concentrated inside, making the internal field strong and uniform. Outside, the field is very weak (practically negligible). Hence option B is correct. Option D is inaccurate because a weak field does exist outside.

mcqs.question: If the current through the coil of an electromagnet is doubled while the number of turns remains the same, how does the magnetic field strength change?
mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field (B) of an electromagnet is directly proportional to the product NI (number of turns times current). Doubling the current (I) while keeping N constant doubles the product, so the field strength also doubles. Therefore option C is correct; the other options misrepresent the proportional relationship.
